summary: prod multiplies numeric items together, beginning with start.
documentation: prod multiplies numeric items together, beginning with start. Its default identity is one, so the product of an empty iterable is one. A zero factor makes the entire product zero.
returns: The integer product of all items, or 1 for an empty list.
caution: An empty product is mathematically one, not zero. Validate domain-specific bounds before using large products in application logic.
scenarios: Compute the number of combinations across independent option counts.
Multiply package dimensions for a volume calculation.
Combine integer multipliers in a manufacturing bill of materials.
title: Multiply independent factors
problem: Return the product of the input integer list. Return 1 for no factors. Values and products stay within the exact JSON integer range.
goal: Use math.prod() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Import prod; an accumulator must start at one.
